system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The agreed baseline is **AUD 24 million for 100% of Paperbark Analytics, debt-free/cash-free, under NSW law**. The recommendations below are buyer-side negotiating positions, not agreed terms. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied, so references require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recoverability; reserve any concession for the overall package. **Reason:** AUD 4.8m may leave substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Individual claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating claims arising from related facts. **Reason:** The proposed combination can exclude meaningful losses and fragment related claims. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer or separate periods for other categories. | **Require 24 months and category-specific exceptions**; ensure timely notification preserves a claim, including contingent claims, without an unduly short proceedings deadline. **Reason:** Eighteen months may not expose issues across two annual reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Standalone protection covering authority, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; no basket or de minimis. | **Require at least a 100% / AUD 24m cap and a six-year contractual notification period**, subject to applicable law and execution form. **Reason:** Failure to acquire valid title to the whole business is not an ordinary operating warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out is identified; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend to all Claims. | Express preservation of fraud claims and remedies, including appropriately attributable fraudulent conduct. | **Exclude fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation from caps, contractual time bars, thresholds, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**, without purporting to override statutory rules. **Reason:** Broad boilerplate must not provide a contractual shield for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against identified warranties. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure**; require specific cross-references and an agreed, frozen disclosure bundle, with any general disclosures tightly defined. **Reason:** Access to a document is not equivalent to meaningful disclosure of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No constructive, imputed or adviser-wide knowledge bar; preferably no separate knowledge exclusion. | **Delete the qualifier**; fallback to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals of the specific breach, with no duty of inquiry and no application to indemnities or fraud. **Reason:** “Discoverable” transfers diligence risk to the Buyer and undermines negotiated warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions. | An effective change-of-control consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, without unacceptable conditions or adverse commercial changes. | **Make effective consent and satisfaction of associated conditions a Buyer-waivable condition precedent**, supported by evidence and a long-stop termination right. **Reason:** Written consent alone may not protect a customer representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repayment and effective release at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Require a verified payout letter, direct payment from Seller proceeds and effective release arrangements at Completion**, including prompt registration steps; do not accept merely a promise of later discharge. **Reason:** The Buyer must not acquire the Company with unpaid debt or continuing lender enforcement exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller calls them its matter. On-cost treatment is unstated. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without double counting. | **Itemise the liability and on-costs in the price adjustment/funds flow**, with a funded retention or indemnity for amounts payable after Completion; confirm employment conditions and payer. **Reason:** Calling a liability “the Seller’s matter” does not prevent the acquired Company bearing it. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; records show **AUD 180,000 open**, but do not independently prove non-payment. Transfer depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. | Verified payment and complete ownership/usage rights, plus protection against residual ownership and infringement exposure from this matter. | **Require payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment/release at or before Completion**, plus a separate indemnity covering resulting claims, remediation and losses—not merely the invoice amount. **Reason:** Paying a recorded balance does not alone establish a complete IP chain of title. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Seller describes it as preliminary and unlikely material; disclosure leaves access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and a properly supported notification assessment, plus protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation and remediation covenants, Buyer reporting and a specific indemnity**, supported by retention/security where appropriate; assess whether unresolved severity warrants a Completion condition. **Reason:** Uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but the record also does not establish a confirmed notifiable breach or quantified loss. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure does not establish that characterisation. | Verification of timing, scope, commitment, termination rights, benefit periods and accounting treatment across DD-008/DD-011. | **Assess the three renewals together and restrict new commitments pending Completion**; allocate through debt, working capital or a specific adjustment only as justified by the facts and agreed definitions. **Reason:** These may be linked commitments, but ordinary future operating expenditure is not automatically Seller debt. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all Claims. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price/payment obligations, covenants and fraud. | **Redraft using an express category matrix and precedence provision**, preserving indemnities, debt recovery, appropriate equitable relief and non-excludable rights. **Reason:** An overarching “all Claims” provision can silently undo every separately negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012’s register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent corroboration of ownership, issued capital, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus effective Completion transfers. | **Reconcile the register with certificates, allotment/transfer records and corporate filings; investigate security and competing rights**, and require transfers, approvals, releases and an updated register at Completion. **Reason:** The register is important evidence, not a substitute for verifying clean title to all issued shares. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled within the general regime. | Separate tax protection for pre-Completion liabilities and suitable tax survival; robust IP warranties and an appropriately longer IP claim period, alongside Ironquay-specific protection. | **Keep both expressly open**: seek a standalone tax indemnity with a separate cap and notification period—initially seven years, checked against relevant assessment rules—and negotiate separate IP survival/cap protection based on diligence. **Reason:** Tax exposures can emerge late, while defective core IP ownership can impair the business well beyond the general warranty period. |

**Priority:** Resolve Bluefen effectiveness, Riverlark discharge, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership before accepting Completion mechanics. Do not allow disclosure or “all Claims” language to neutralise the resulting protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
